_comment: Single source of truth for release packaging, the web flasher and the CLI. Keys are PlatformIO env names. mcu/radio/display/extras/status are what the board matrix in docs/hardware.md shows; tools/board_docs.py renders it from here.
_local_link: Per-board host connectivity, read by tools/board_caps.py into BOARD_* build flags and by the settings API. usb.native = the MCU's own D+/D- reach the connector; usb.ncm/cdc_acm = the silicon could present those classes there (whether this firmware build does is LOCAL_LINK_USB_NCM); usb.auto_reset_dtr_rts = esptool can reset the chip through this port without BOOT being held; uart.network = the UART behind the bridge may carry PPP (LOCAL_LINK_PPP says whether the build does); uart.tested_max_baud = the highest rate qualified on hardware, rts/cts = flow-control lines the bridge exposes to the chip.

_usb_identity._comment: What the S3's composite USB device (CDC-ACM console + CDC-NCM network) says it is. tools/board_caps.py hands these to the core as USB_VID/USB_PID/USB_MANUFACTURER/USB_PRODUCT; the host tool recognises the pair and the product string; the serial number is the factory MAC. 1209:0001 is pid.codes' test allocation, permitted for development and forbidden for anything shipped; an Espressif PID under 0x303A is requested per github.com/espressif/usb-pids.

t3s3.name: LilyGO T3-S3 v1.2/v1.3 (SX1262 or SX1276/78)
t3s3.notes: 0.96" OLED, 4 MB flash, 2 MB PSRAM. The transceiver (SX1262 or SX1276/78) is detected at boot. Native USB — hold BOOT while pressing RST if the port is not detected.

esp32s3-qspi.name: Generic ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 + SX1262 module
esp32s3-qspi.notes: 8 MB flash, quad PSRAM. Wire the SX1262 as documented in platformio.ini (PIN_LORA_* overrides).

tbeam.name: LilyGO T-Beam v1.1/v1.2 (SX1276 or SX1262)
tbeam.extras: 18650 holder, AXP192/AXP2101 PMU, u-blox GPS; **no SD slot**
tbeam.status: verified on hardware — see the T-Beam notes below
tbeam.notes: 18650 holder, AXP192/AXP2101 power management, u-blox GPS, 0.96" OLED, no SD card slot. The transceiver and the PMU revision are both detected at boot. Serial is a CH9102 bridge — hold the middle button while pressing RST if flashing does not start.

t3s3-sx1280.name: LilyGO T3-S3 with SX1280 (2.4 GHz)
t3s3-sx1280.notes: 0.96" OLED, SD slot, 4 MB flash. The plain SX1280 module: no power amplifier, so the chip's 13 dBm ceiling applies. The amplified variant is a different image — see t3s3-sx1280-pa. The radio is selected at build time rather than detected, so neither is interchangeable with the sub-GHz t3s3 build. Defaults to 2445 MHz / 812.5 kHz / SF8.

t3s3-sx1280-pa.name: LilyGO T3-S3 with SX1280 + PA (2.4 GHz)
t3s3-sx1280-pa.status: **builds only — never run on hardware**, see below
t3s3-sx1280-pa.notes: As t3s3-sx1280, but for the amplified module: the PA sits behind an RX/TX switch on GPIO 21/10 and the ceiling rises to 20 dBm. Flashing this image on a plain board would drive two GPIOs that board uses for something else, so pick by what is actually fitted.

heltec-ws.name: Heltec Wireless Stick V2/V2.1
heltec-ws.notes: 0.49" 64x32 OLED on the switched Vext rail, SX1276, 8 MB flash, no SD slot and no GNSS. The small panel gets its own page layout — ten columns and four rows — rather than the 128x64 one clipped. Serial is a CP2102 bridge, and every CP2102 reports the serial number 0001, so with more than one attached /dev/serial/by-id/ names only one of them and the rest have to be found by path. Uses the 8 MB partition table for the same reason the V3 does: no SD card, so the filesystem is the only storage the transport store has.

heltec-wb.name: Heltec Wireless Bridge
heltec-wb.extras: front LEDs for Wi-Fi and LoRa (the BLE one stays dark), aluminium shell, two SMA sockets, internal 2-pin battery connector; no SD, no GNSS
heltec-wb.notes: The Wireless Stick's ESP32 and SX1276 in an aluminium box with two SMA antenna sockets, 8 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM, no display, no SD slot and no GNSS: a headless relay. Serial is a CP2102 bridge on the micro-USB socket, and every CP2102 reports the serial number 0001, so with more than one attached /dev/serial/by-id/ names only one of them and the rest have to be found by path. Uses the 8 MB partition table: no SD card, so the filesystem is the only storage the transport store has.

heltec-v3.name: Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V3
heltec-v3.radio: SX1262 (TCXO, DIO2 drives the RF switch)
heltec-v3.display: 0.96" SSD1306 on the switched Vext rail
heltec-v3.notes: 0.96" 128x64 OLED on the switched Vext rail, SX1262 with a TCXO, 8 MB flash and no PSRAM, no SD slot and no GNSS. Very common hardware. A CP2102 bridge rather than the S3's native USB, so it appears as /dev/ttyUSB* and not as an Espressif JTAG device — and every CP2102 reports the serial number 0001, so with more than one attached /dev/serial/by-id/ names only one of them and the rest have to be found by path. Uses an 8 MB partition table: the stock one maps only the first 4 MB, and with no SD card the filesystem is the only storage the transport store has.
